blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Few topics in contemporary management generate as much noise and as little useful signal as executive pay. Investors, employees, regulators and the public all hold strong views, and those views rarely align with each other. Designing compensation in this environment is a genuinely difficult act of judgement, as much as of analysis.

The core tension is between incentive and unintended consequence. Well-designed variable pay can reliably align individual effort with collective outcomes; poorly designed variable pay can incentivise exactly the behaviours the board most feared. The history of corporate scandal is, quite disproportionately, a history of incentive schemes that worked precisely as they were designed to — in ways no one intended.

Pay transparency is a newer front in the debate. While full transparency has obvious advantages for trust and equity, it can also harden disputes, entrench status concerns and complicate the judgement that inevitably sits behind any individual decision. Thoughtful organisations are now experimenting with partial transparency — clear principles and ranges, without fully public individual amounts — as a balance between openness and pragmatism.

items.q: According to the text, why is designing executive compensation so difficult?
options: It requires judgement as well as analysis, amid stakeholders whose views rarely align
Regulators change the rules every year
There is no reliable data on pay
items.why: "a genuinely difficult act of judgement, as much as of analysis" — e os pontos de vista raramente se alinham.

items.q: What is described as "the core tension" in pay design?
items.why: "The core tension is between incentive and unintended consequence."

items.q: The author suggests that most corporate scandals happened because incentive schemes…
options: worked exactly as designed, producing effects no one intended
were too generous to junior staff
items.why: Inferência: "schemes that worked precisely as they were designed to — in ways no one intended" — o problema é o desenho, não a falha de execução.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Full pay transparency is unambiguously the best policy in every case
Compensation involves judgement, not just formulas
Partial transparency can balance openness and pragmatism
items.why: Inferência: o texto elogia a transparência, mas alerta que ela endurece disputas — logo, discordaria de que seja sempre a melhor opção.

items.q: What does the preference for "partial transparency" imply about the author's view?
options: That secrecy is always preferable to disclosure
That the trade-offs of full disclosure are real and worth managing carefully
That transparency has no benefits at all
That individual pay should always be made public
items.why: Inferência: propor um meio-termo pressupõe reconhecer custos reais dos dois extremos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando o comitê de remuneração. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making time. Before we touch a single number, I want to be clear about what shareholders were actually objecting to at the last say-on-pay vote. It wasn't the quantum. It was the fact that the long-term incentive paid out in full during a year when the share price barely moved. That is the perception we have to fix.

So here is what I would put to the committee. First, we lengthen the vesting horizon from three years to five. If we are calling it a long-term incentive, it should behave like one. Second, and this is non-negotiable in my view, we introduce a proper clawback clause. If the numbers that triggered a payout are later restated, the board can recover the award. That is our insurance against exactly the kind of unintended outcome that gets companies onto the front page.

On transparency, I am going to resist the temptation to publish individual figures. Instead, we disclose the principles and the pay bands. People will know how the machine works, and where they sit within it, without every individual amount becoming a source of grievance.

None of this is a formula. It is a judgement. But it is a defensible one, and right now, defensible is precisely what we need.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Charlotte, what were shareholders actually objecting to?
options: The total size of the pay package
That the long-term incentive paid out in full while the share price barely moved
The lack of any bonus scheme
items.why: "It wasn't the quantum. It was the fact that the long-term incentive paid out in full during a year when the share price barely moved."

items.q: What change does she propose to the vesting horizon?
options: Shorten it from five years to three
Lengthen it from three years to five
items.why: "we lengthen the vesting horizon from three years to five."

items.q: Why does Charlotte call the clawback clause the board's "insurance"?
options: It reduces the cost of the scheme
It lets the board recover awards if the triggering numbers are later restated
It guarantees a minimum payout to executives
It replaces the need for shareholder votes
items.why: "If the numbers that triggered a payout are later restated, the board can recover the award." — protege contra consequências não intencionais.

items.q: What can you infer about Charlotte's stance on transparency?
options: She wants every individual figure published for full accountability
She favours disclosing principles and pay bands, but not individual amounts
She opposes disclosing any information at all
She thinks transparency is irrelevant to the redesign
items.why: Inferência: ela resiste a publicar números individuais e prefere divulgar princípios e faixas — transparência parcial.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean when she says "defensible is precisely what we need"?
options: The plan must be cheap above all else
The board needs a decision it can justify publicly, even if it is a judgement rather than a formula
The committee should avoid making any decision
The plan should be kept secret from shareholders
items.why: Inferência: depois da pressão dos acionistas, ela busca uma escolha que a diretoria consiga defender publicamente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The scandal was a textbook unintended consequence of a well-meant bonus." This describes…
options: an outcome nobody intended but the design produced anyway
a mistake in the payroll system
a decision to cancel the bonus
items.why: Unintended consequence = consequência não intencional — resultado que ninguém quis, mas que o desenho gerou.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Rather than publish exact figures, we disclosed each role's ___ so people knew the range they sat within."
items.why: Pay band = faixa salarial — o intervalo de remuneração de um cargo.

items.q: "The contract included a clawback clause." A clawback allows the company to…
options: increase the award automatically each year
recover money already paid if results are later restated
items.why: Clawback = cláusula de recuperação — permite reaver valores já pagos em certas condições.

items.q: "At the AGM, investors exercised their say on pay." This refers to…
options: an advisory shareholder vote on executive remuneration
the executives' right to negotiate their salaries
a regulator's power to cap bonuses
items.why: Say on pay = voto consultivo dos acionistas sobre a remuneração dos executivos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Making individual amounts public risked inflaming ___ among peers who felt unfairly ranked."
items.why: Status concern = questão de status — a preocupação com posição relativa que a divulgação pode acirrar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de comitê de remuneração. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee will have to sign off on the revised plan before the AGM." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A block of shareholders pushed back on the payout structure." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Tinkering with the bonus multiplier won't move the needle on retention." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed the clawback in principle, but no one followed through on the drafting." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, o que faltou.

items.q: "Let's not lose sight of what the vote was really about." To lose sight of something means to…
options: stop paying attention to it or forget its importance
items.why: Lose sight of = perder de vista, deixar de considerar algo importante.
